comparisons.note: two peaks 0.9% apart: RocketPy's are 111.18 m/s^2 on the rail at 0.05 s and 112.26 at 1.568 s, so its maximum is the later one; hpr's rail equation adds 1.16 m/s^2 of variable-mass terms at 0.05 s (thrust and mass equal to five digits), which lifts that peak to 112.35 and moves the maximum's time from one peak to the other. The value itself is gated and agrees to 0.07%.

the whole flight's maximum is the main parachute opening at 54.9 s (191.8 m/s^2 in RocketPy, 300.9 in hpr), not a flight load; RocketPy adds the canopy's added mass while it opens and hpr has none (ADR-012), which is a known difference in the opening transient, not in the flight. The power-on maximum is gated instead.

gaps.reason: The reference peaks at Mach 1.014 near burnout, and hpr's aerodynamics refuse M >= 1 until M1.8 (ADR-008, ADR-011), so the flight stops at Mach 1 and no metric can be compared.
gaps.refusal: refused the flight at Mach 1.000, outside its subsonic models' range of [0, 1)
